newsitem.title: USA: CPI-linked corporate debt tops $1.0 bln on week.
newsitem.headline: CPI-linked corporate debt tops $1.0 bln on week.

text.p: A $450 million five-year CPI-linked debt issue from Salomon Inc on Friday, pushed the volume of indexed bonds over $1.0 billion on the week, and that trend was expected to accelerate, dealers said.
The novel security was sold primarily to money managers with a minority amount distributed to insurance companies, said Nestor Dominguez, vice president of Salomon Brothers' debt syndicate desk.
Salomon's issue, increased first from $250 million and then from $400 million, was priced to yield 65 basis points over the Treasury's 10-year inflation indexed note.

The notes, rated Baa1/BBB, were the first of their kind to be issued outside the "A" credit range. Tennessee Valley Authority (Aaa/AAA) on Wednesday issued $300 million; Toyota Motor Credit Corp (Aaa/AAA) on Thursday issued $100 million; and J.P. Morgan & Co (Aa3/AA) on Thursday issued $200 million.
Government agencies such as the Federal Home Loan Bank System have also issued CPI-linked debt.

Syndicate officials said investors are rapidly warming to the new asset class and expect the calendar to build as the market's liquidity rises. Extensions in ratings, from AAAs to lower investment grades, should be expected, they added.
"I think investors see this as a new asset category," Dominguez said. "They're becoming more and more familiar with the product and it'll become easier to trade and understand."
Dominguez said the Treasury has indicated it will calculate a dual index should there be a recalculation of CPI in the future, immunizing the bonds from changes in the index.
Still, some buysiders said they had just begun assessing the securities and said the future was uncertain.
Other high-grade corporate debt tracked Treasuries higher in thin trade, following a bond-friendly U.S. employment report. Tele-Communications debt firmed by two basis points.
Turning to high-yielders, several high-yield issues dominated the scene in an otherwise quiet session, traders there said.

-- Acindar Industria Argentina de Aceros' $100 million deal led issuance on Friday. The deal, priced at par to yield 11-1/4 percent or 491 basis points over the U.S. Treasury curve, came 25 to 50 basis points through earlier speculation.
Credit Suisse First Boston was lead manager.
-- International CableTel Inc priced $400 million 10-year senior notes at 347 basis points over the T-note and $100 million exchangeable preferreds of '09 at a 13 percent yield.
Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette was lead manager.

Outstanding International CableTel bonds traded unchanged to firmer as the issue priced, traders said. The zero coupon debt due 2006, which fell about two points when the new deal was announced two weeks ago, traded flat at 67-1/4.
The new senior notes were seen bid up 1/4 point at the close, one trader said.

-- Optel Inc priced $225 million overfunded senior notes due 2005 to yield 13 percent via Salomon Brothers. The issue priced at the wide side of price talk and was sold with warrants for five percent of the company, a trader said.
Noting heavy roadshow calendars, dealers braced for a heavier slate of new issues next week.
In the Treassury market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed off its highs but up 23/32 to yield 6.70 percent.
